description: Heritage reporter-alias diagnostic identity is CANONICAL, not the surface spelling (issue #733). With Heritage active, the parenthesized reporter alias `(bf)` under-applies `butfirst` (arity 1, given 0) and is caught by the semantic checker's arity rule (`checker-arity.ts`). Diagnostic identity is `code` plus structured `params`, and those params carry the CANONICAL Core name (`spec/error-model.md:255-260`): `params.callable` is `"butfirst"` — byte-identical to the diagnostic `print (butfirst)` raises — never the surface alias `"bf"`. Heritage is "alternate spellings only, no new semantics" (`spec/conformance.md#heritage`); a machine-readable param whose value changed with the spelling would be an observable semantic difference, exactly the divergence H5 (#670) closed for its `operation` param. This fixture asserts `params.callable` directly — the absence of such a fixture is what let the surface-spelling regression ship (M4 audit finding F3: an unasserted field is an unprotected one).
